name: Meteorites
description: Solid extraterrestrial fragments that survive atmospheric passage; classified by mineralogy, petrography, bulk chemistry and O-isotopes into chondrites, primitive achondrites and achondrites.

name: Chondrites
description: Undifferentiated meteorites with broadly solar (CI-like) bulk compositions minus the most volatile elements, from bodies that never underwent planetary melting; most contain chondrules. 15 groups across the C, O and E classes plus R and K.

name: Primitive achondrites
description: Nonchondritic meteorites with igneous or recrystallized textures that retain a chemical/isotopic affinity to chondritic precursors; interpreted as residues or low-degree partial melts that did not fully differentiate.

name: Achondrites
description: Differentiated meteorites - igneous rocks, melt residues, or breccias of igneous fragments - from asteroids, Mars and the Moon that experienced a high degree of melting; includes stones, stony-irons and irons.

name: Carbonaceous chondrites
description: Chondrite class with Mg-normalized refractory-lithophile abundances at or above CI and O-isotopes plotting near or below the terrestrial fractionation line; eight groups.

name: Ordinary chondrites
description: The most abundant chondrites (>85% of falls); abundant large chondrules, low matrix, refractory-lithophile abundances below CI, O-isotopes above the TF line. The three groups form one clan.

name: Enstatite chondrites
description: Chondrites formed under highly reducing conditions, with Fe-poor silicates, Si-bearing metal and unusual sulfides/nitrides; O-isotopes on the TF line near Earth and the Moon. Two groups.

name: CI clan
description: Single-group clan; CI chondrites show nothing linking them to the other carbonaceous clans.

name: CM-CO clan
description: Clan linking the CM and CO groups by similar chondrule sizes, refractory-lithophile abundances, and high-temperature-mineral O-isotopes.

name: CV-CK clan
description: Clan grouping CV and CK chondrites, which share overlapping CCAM-line O-isotopes and magnetite chemistry; low-type CK resembles oxidized CV.

name: CR clan
description: Clan of the metal-rich CR, CH and CB groups (plus ungrouped LEW 85332), united by solar-Ni/Co metal, strong volatile-lithophile depletions, CR-line O-isotopes, and large d15N anomalies.

name: CI (Ivuna-type)
description: Ivuna-type; among the most primitive solar-system materials, bulk composition close to the solar photosphere. All petrologic type 1: heavily hydrated, brecciated, chondrule- and CAI-free phyllosilicate-rich rocks.

name: CM (Mighei-type)
description: Mighei-type; the most abundant C chondrites. Small (~300 um) chondrules, abundant matrix, CAIs/AOAs partly replaced by phyllosilicates; mostly aqueously altered type 2 (some type 1).

name: CO (Ornans-type)
description: Ornans-type; small (~150 um) chondrules with 30-45 vol% matrix; petrologic types 3.0-3.7, O-isotopes on the CCAM line overlapping CV.

name: CV (Vigarano-type)
description: Vigarano-type; abundant matrix, large (~1 mm) chondrules and abundant large CAIs/AOAs; all type 3, divided into oxidized and reduced subgroups.

name: CK (Karoonda-type)
description: Karoonda-type; matrix-rich with large (700-1000 um) porphyritic chondrules; highly oxidized (fayalitic olivine, abundant magnetite), mostly high petrologic type 4-6.

name: CR (Renazzo-type)
description: Renazzo-type; mostly type 2, with large metal-rich porphyritic Mg-rich chondrules with multilayered rims, hydrated matrix, solar-Ni/Co metal, and large d15N.

name: CH (high-metal)
description: ALH 85085-type; high metal (~20 vol%), tiny (<100 um) mostly cryptocrystalline chondrules, virtually no matrix, very large d15N anomalies.

name: CB (Bencubbin-type)
description: Bencubbin-type; extreme metal (60-80 vol%), cryptocrystalline/barred chondrules, strong volatile-lithophile depletion and heavy-N enrichment; subgroups CBa and CBb.

name: CV subgroup A (oxidized, Allende-like)
description: Oxidized Allende-like CV (CVoxA); secondary ferrous olivine, Ca,Fe-pyroxene, andradite and nepheline/sodalite, coarser matrix than CVoxB with only minor phyllosilicates.

name: CV subgroup B (oxidized, Bali-like)
description: Oxidized Bali-like CV (CVoxB); aqueously altered with abundant phyllosilicates, magnetite, fayalite and Ca,Fe-pyroxenes; highest matrix/chondrule ratio.

name: CV subgroup (reduced)
description: Reduced CV (CVred); lowest matrix/chondrule and highest metal/magnetite ratios, with only minor nepheline/sodalite and Ca,Fe-pyroxenes.

name: CB subgroup a
description: CBa; ~60 vol% metal, centimeter-sized chondrules, metal with 5-8 wt% Ni, d15N up to ~1000 per mil.

name: CB subgroup b
description: CBb; >70 vol% metal, millimeter-sized chondrules, metal with 4-15 wt% Ni, d15N ~200 per mil; argued to be the more primitive nebular endmember.

name: H-L-LL clan
description: Single ordinary-chondrite clan; H, L and LL overlap in O-isotopes and petrology, indicating close kinship.

name: H (high iron)
description: Highest total Fe and metallic-Fe/FeO ratio among O chondrites; equilibrated olivine Fa16-20.

name: L (low iron)
description: Intermediate Fe content among O chondrites; equilibrated olivine Fa23-26.

name: LL (low iron, low metal)
description: Lowest Fe and metal among O chondrites; equilibrated olivine Fa27-32.

name: EH-EL clan
description: Single enstatite-chondrite clan; EH and EL are distinguished mainly by sulfide chemistry and metal Si content.

name: EH (high iron)
description: High-Fe enstatite chondrites; more reduced, niningerite-bearing, with Si-rich (2-3 wt%) metal.

name: EL (low iron)
description: Low-Fe enstatite chondrites; alabandite-bearing, <1 wt% Si in metal, ranging to higher petrologic types (EL6).

name: R (Rumuruti-type)
description: Rumuruti-type; highly oxidized, FeO-rich olivine (Fa37-40), nearly metal-free, ~50% matrix; highest delta-17O of any chondrite group; affiliated with but distinct from the O class (possibly a separate class or O clan).
notes: Connects directly to Chondrites in figure (no class/clan box)

name: K (Kakangari-type)
description: Kakangari-type grouplet; chemically, mineralogically and isotopically distinct from the C, O and E classes; high matrix, Fe-poor olivine/enstatite, O-isotopes below the TF line; a candidate first member of a fourth chondrite class.
notes: Connects directly to Chondrites in figure (no class/clan box)

name: Ureilite
description: Ureilites; olivine-pyroxene rocks with interstitial graphite/diamond, metal and sulfides and reduced olivine rims; O-isotopes scatter along the CCAM line. Interpreted as partial-melt residues / mantle rock of the ureilite parent body.
notes: Connects directly to Primitive Achondrites (no clan box)

name: Brachinite
description: Brachinites; medium- to coarse-grained, olivine-rich (74-98%) equigranular achondrites with near-chondritic lithophile abundances; debated origin as residues, cumulates, or recrystallized chondritic material.
notes: Connects directly to Primitive Achondrites (no clan box)

name: Acapulcoite-Lodranite clan
description: Acapulcoite-Lodranite clan; primitive achondrites with similar, spread O-isotopes; residues/products of low-degree partial melting of a chondritic precursor.

name: Acapulcoite
description: Acapulcoites; fine-grained (150-230 um) equigranular rocks with near-chondritic mineral abundances and rare relict chondrules; formed by very low-degree partial melting (~950 C).

name: Lodranite
description: Lodranites; coarse-grained (540-700 um) olivine-pyroxene rocks depleted in plagioclase and troilite; residues of higher-degree partial melting (~1250 C) with basaltic-melt removal.

name: Winonaite-IAB-IIICD clan
description: Winonaite-IAB-IIICD clan; silicate mineralogy and O-isotopes link winonaites to silicate inclusions in IAB (and possibly IIICD) irons, implying a shared or similar parent body.

name: Winonaite
description: Winonaites; chondritic mineralogy/composition but recrystallized achondritic textures; mineral compositions between E and H chondrites, with Fe,Ni-FeS veins recording first partial melts.

name: IAB iron (silicate-bearing)
description: Silicate-bearing iron group whose inclusions resemble winonaites in mineralogy and O-isotopes; historically called 'nonmagmatic,' with textures suggesting impact mixing of metal and silicate. Wasson & Kallemeyn (2002) merge IAB+IIICD as the 'IAB complex.'

name: IIICD iron (silicate-bearing)
description: Silicate-bearing iron group historically paired with IAB; Wasson & Kallemeyn (2002) treat IAB+IIICD as a single IAB complex. Geochemical trends differ from the magmatic groups.

name: Angrite
description: Angrites; vesicular basaltic igneous rocks with unusual Ca-Al-Ti-rich pyroxene, Ca-rich olivine and anorthitic plagioclase - the most alkali-depleted basalts known; O-isotopes near HED but mineralogically distinct.

name: Aubrite
description: Aubrites (enstatite achondrites); highly reduced, brecciated rocks of nearly FeO-free enstatite with E-chondrite-like sulfides; likely linked to, but from a different parent body than, the EL chondrites.

name: Mesosiderite
description: Mesosiderites; stony-iron breccias of roughly equal silicate (basalt/gabbro/pyroxenite clasts) and Fe,Ni-metal+troilite, with metal intimately mixed with similarly sized silicate grains.

name: HED clan (Vesta)
description: HED clan (howardites-eucrites-diogenites); basalts and orthopyroxene cumulates from a common asteroidal parent, sharing O-isotopes and pyroxene Fe/Mn; spectrally linked to asteroid 4 Vesta.
notes: howardite-eucrite-diogenite; parent body inferred as Vesta

name: Eucrite
description: Eucrites; basalts of plagioclase and clinopyroxene (pyroxene Fe/Mn ~30) from near-surface flows or intrusives; commonly brecciated.

name: Diogenite
description: Diogenites; coarse orthopyroxene cumulates from deeper plutonic levels of the HED parent body.

name: Howardite
description: Howardites; polymict regolith breccias mixing eucritic and diogenitic clasts.

name: Pallasites
description: Pallasites; olivine-metal (+troilite) stony-irons. 'Pallasite' is essentially a textural term: the main-group, Eagle Station and pyroxene pallasites (plus ungrouped Milton) formed on separate parent bodies and do not form a true clan/group.
notes: Unlabeled shared connector in figure (clan-row grouping)

name: Main-group pallasite
description: Main-group pallasites; olivine-metal rocks whose metal resembles Ni-rich IIIAB irons and whose O-isotopes match the HEDs (no proven genetic link).

name: Eagle Station pallasite
description: Eagle Station grouplet; more ferroan, Ca-rich olivine and distinct O-isotopes; metal resembles IIF irons (higher Ni and Ir).

name: Pyroxene pallasite
description: Pyroxene-pallasite grouplet (e.g., Vermillion, Y-8451); contain mm-sized pyroxene, with metal and O-isotopes distinguishing them from the other pallasites.

name: Irons
description: Iron meteorites; mostly cores of differentiated asteroids. The chemical classification (Scott & Wasson) uses Ga, Ge, Ir and Ni - a Roman numeral plus a letter - resolving 13 groups; ~10 are consistent with fractional crystallization in separate cores, and ~15% of irons (40% in Antarctica) are ungrouped.
source: Weisberg et al. (2006); Scott & Wasson (1975); Wasson iron-classification series
notes: Unlabeled shared connector in figure (clan-row grouping)

name: IC iron group
description: Magmatic iron group resolved on Ga/Ge-Ni plots; interpreted as a fractionally crystallized asteroid core.

name: IIAB iron group
description: Largest magmatic iron group (hexahedrites/coarse octahedrites); a fractional-crystallization trend from a single core.

name: IIC iron group
description: Magmatic iron group with a traditional core-crystallization history.

name: IID iron group
description: Magmatic iron group formed by fractional crystallization in an asteroid core.

name: IIE iron group
description: Silicate-bearing iron group; some silicates resemble H chondrites. Historically 'nonmagmatic,' with poorly defined elemental trends suggesting impact mixing of metal and silicate.
source: Weisberg et al. (2006); Scott & Wasson (1975); Wasson iron-classification series

name: IIIAB iron group
description: One of the largest magmatic iron groups (octahedrites); a single fractional-crystallization sequence (former IIIA+IIIB), with metal close to main-group-pallasite composition.

name: IIIE iron group
description: Magmatic iron group resembling IIIA/IIIAB but resolved by lower Ga/Ni and Ge/Ni, larger kamacite bandwidths, and haxonite (carbide) in its members.

name: IIIF iron group
description: Small, volatile-depleted (low Ga/Ge) magmatic iron group, distinct from IIIAB.

name: IVA iron group
description: Volatile-depleted magmatic iron group (fine octahedrites) with a range of cooling rates, suggesting metal pods at varying depths in a partially molten body.

name: IVB iron group
description: Most volatile-depleted iron group; metal matches a high-temperature (~1270 K) nebular condensate, implying high-temperature accretion.

name: Lunar (Moon)
description: Lunar meteorites; rocks launched from the Moon, sharing mineralogy/Fe-Mn and O-isotopes with Apollo/Luna samples but sampling random sites (including the farside). Mainly feldspathic-highland breccias, mare basalts/breccias, and mingled breccias.
source: Weisberg et al. (2006); lunar meteorite literature (Korotev; Lunar Meteorite Compendium)
notes: No group boxes shown in figure

name: Martian (SNC)
description: Martian (SNC) meteorites; crustal igneous rocks from Mars defining a unique slope-0.52 O-isotope line, with trapped gases matching the martian atmosphere. Includes shergottites, nakhlites, chassignites and orthopyroxenite ALH 84001.

name: Shergottite
description: Shergottites; basaltic and lherzolitic/olivine-phyric volcanic-plutonic rocks, mostly young (<1.3 Ga); the most abundant martian meteorites.

name: Nakhlite
description: Nakhlites; clinopyroxene (augite)-rich cumulate rocks from Mars.

name: Chassignite
description: Chassignites; olivine-rich (dunitic) cumulate martian rocks (e.g., Chassigny).

name: Orthopyroxenite
description: Orthopyroxenite represented by ALH 84001, a ~4.5 Ga coarse orthopyroxene cumulate from Mars, originally misclassified as a diogenite.
